title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-fibration in algebraic geometry and $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy type
summary: In this article we show that an $\mathbb{A}^1$ bundle map or a vector bundle map $p: X \to Y$ induces trivial local fibration $\underline{Sing}(X) \to \underline{Sing}(Y)$. Using this, we first show that for Korus Russel threefolds of first kind $X$ the space $\underline{Sing}(X)$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$ local. Then we show that for any smooth affine complex surface $X$, the $\mathbb{A}^1$- connected component sheaf is homotopy invariant.
